{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"“The fox found the moon,” Elsie said, “but it was too heavy to carry home.”

The little figure listened, his leaf coat rustling though the room was still. Mara glanced at their mother. She had gone very pale, but she was smiling, too.

“So the fox asked the stars for help,” their mother continued. “They made a ladder of their light.”

At that, the golden thread brightened. It ran through the roof of the tiny house and up into the roots above. The wooden walls shivered. A window opened, and warm yellow light spilled across the floor.

The figure looked at their mother. “You remember the next part.”

She shook her head. “I remember a voice singing. I thought I’d dreamed it.”

“Then sing it now,” he said.

For a moment, she said nothing. Then she hummed a tune Mara knew from bedtime, though she had never heard its ending. Elsie joined in, and the paper boat lifted from the thread. It floated around the room, its blue bird shining bright as a flame.

A tiny silver moon appeared in the boat.

The figure reached for it, but stopped. “It belongs to the story,” he said. “Stories need somewhere to go.”

Mara understood. She took the boat and set it in the little house’s open window. The moon drifted out, up the golden thread, and vanished among the roots.

Above them, the pear tree gave a soft, happy shiver.

Their mother stepped forward. “Can you come with us?”

The figure looked toward the stairs. “Not yet,” he said. “But now you know where to find me.”

And from somewhere deep in the house, a new story began to knock."}
